card.name: Units right after a number or range
card.fires_on: The unit or symbol that follows a number, especially the degree mark or F in a Fahrenheit range such as 59°F to 77°F. It also fires on page-range letters, M abbreviations and quantity units like gallons.

modes.label: Fahrenheit in temperature range
modes.description: The degree sign or F after a Fahrenheit number inside parentheses in storage temperatures.
modes.example: constituted product may be stored for up to 12 hours at room temperature (15°C to 25°C; 59<<°F>> to 77°F).

modes.label: Other units after numbers
modes.description: Quantity words, abbreviations or marks after a figure, such as gallons, MM or minutes.
modes.example: One ton saves the equivalent of 24 trees, 7,000<< gallons>> of water

modes.label: Page-range letter
modes.description: A letter attached to a page number in a citation.

card.plain: It marks the unit right after a number, most often the Fahrenheit part of a room-temperature range.
